note: [agent-bulk] Clean nuecc single-shower event. shw 16008 (236.3 MeV, 4 seg, 37.9 cm, conn 1) starts ON the vertex - its seed segment 16008 runs from 19.6 cm out down to (18.5,-39.2,92.6), which is the main vertex to 0.1 cm, so the X and the blue star coincide in both shower frames. On shw16008-az-055-el+20 and -az+085-el+20 it is one continuous object rising from the star, broadening steadily, its yellow halo covering the whole body and its point cloud, one apex, one direction. Nothing is missing: apart from its own members (16010 at 19.6 cm / 4.0 deg and 16001 at 27.4 cm / 9.0 deg, both in_main_cluster) every candidate within 70 cm is at 32-135 deg from the axis and none is bigger than 1.2 cm - there is no unclaimed charge in the cone. THE ONE THING I WOULD QUERY, and it is why the confidence is likely rather than certain: member 42016 is a 0.41 cm pdg-13 dot at 66.7 cm / 13.2 deg, absorbed by pass3_cone, and it sits about 30 cm BEYOND the end of the shower body with empty space in between - visible on both azimuths as a lone yellow-haloed dot far from everything else. Marked OUT. The charge is negligible so I do NOT call the event over-clustered on it; the verdict is about the shower body, which is right. Be aware this reproduces the roll-up tension pr/116 section 5 records: an OUT mark on a member is read by pr/115 rule 3 as a remove-this statement and would bucket this event under over-clustering, which is not what I mean here. Vertex: on vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits at the base of the shower and the rest of the event is a scatter of sub-cm dots - there is no competing prong, so nothing contradicts the star, but equally nothing independently confirms it beyond the shower's own start. Scope: 1 shower of 19 examined; 18 skipped by the <20 MeV rule and not looked at. The vtx-* sweep is half-span 84 cm and was used for topology only. No reco pi0 in this event (pio_grp=0, pio_id=-1, and the capture emitted no pi0 slots), and there is no second EM object anywhere to pair with. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
